prerequisites: A good level of knowledge of mathematics and physics, technical thermodynamics, heat transfer and fluid mechanics.

learning_outcomes.text: Students should be able to apply the acquired knowledge and their problem-solving capacity in new or little-known environments within broader (or multidisciplinary) contexts related to their field of study.

Students should be able to integrate knowledge and face the complexity of formulating judgments based on incomplete or limited information, including reflections on the social and ethical responsibilities linked to the application of their knowledge and judgments.
Students should be able to communicate their conclusions and the knowledge and ultimate reasons that support them to specialized and non-specialized audiences in a clear and unambiguous way.
Students should possess the learning skills that allow them to continue studying in a largely self-directed or autonomous way.

Possess adequate knowledge of the scientific and technological aspects of: mathematical, analytical and numerical methods in engineering, electrical engineering, energy engineering, chemical engineering, mechanical engineering, continuum mechanics, industrial electronics, automation, manufacturing, materials, quantitative management methods, industrial informatics, urban planning and infrastructures.
Plan, calculate and design products, processes, facilities and plants.
Achieve the ability to integrate knowledge to formulate development applications of new energy technologies.
Carry out research, development and innovation in products, processes and methods.
Carry out strategic planning and apply it to construction, production, quality and environmental management systems.
Knowledge, understanding and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Engineer.
Knowledge and skills for the design and analysis of thermal machines and engines, hydraulic machines and industrial heating and cooling installations.
Knowledge about construction, building, installations, infrastructures and urban planning in the field of industrial engineering.

Knowledge and skills for planning and designing electrical and fluid installations, lighting, air conditioning and ventilation, energy saving and efficiency, acoustics, communications, home automation and intelligent buildings and security installations.
Knowledge and skills to carry out verification and control of installations, processes and products.
Apply air control techniques to achieve thermal comfort conditions in air-conditioned buildings.
Design and dimension the main elements of air conditioning systems and refrigeration installations, based on thermal load calculation.

Understand the most common air conditioning systems, the most energy-efficient designs and strategies for building air conditioning, heating and domestic hot water production, as well as advanced applications of the vapor compression refrigeration cycle.

Apply the energy efficiency, safety and environmental parameters that condition the use and replacement of working fluids in refrigeration installations according to current legislation and regulations.
Calculate and size evaporative cooling systems.

syllabus_topics: Sizing of air conditioning and refrigeration systems: Thermal load calculations.
Cold production and distribution systems. Refrigerant fluids.
Air conditioning, heating, and domestic hot water systems and technologies.
teaching_methods: Virtual Campus activities (reading theoretical foundations, participation in discussion forums, viewing additional material)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, if the written exam score (EX) is 3.5 or higher, the final grade is calculated as (0.25 * PL) + (0.25 * PA) + (0.5 * EX). If the written exam score is below 3.5, the final grade is EX. For extraordinary calls, the final grade is (0.2 * PL) + (0.8 * EX), where PL is the continuous assessment grade. For students with differentiated evaluation, the final grade is EX. To pass the course, the final grade must be 5.0 or higher.
